summary.headline: Surya Roshni Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 33% YoY to INR2,448 crores, but EBITDA grew only 1% to INR143 crores as steel EBITDA/ton stayed near INR4,100.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue hit a record INR2,448 crores (+33% YoY, +20% QoQ), driven by steel pipe volumes of 2.67 lakh tons (+23% YoY) and lighting revenue of INR507 crores (+17% YoY). Consolidated EBITDA of INR143 crores was flat YoY and PAT of INR77 crores rose 3%, as steel EBITDA/ton fell to INR4,105 from INR5,013 a year earlier. Management guided to a sharp steel EBITDA/ton recovery in H2 (INR4,800-4,900 in Q3, above INR5,000 in Q4) and reiterated FY27 volume of 11 lakh tons. The company remains debt-free with INR75 crores cash surplus, and a share buyback was discussed but not announced.

segments.name: Steel Pipes and Strips
segments.commentary: Q2 volume a record 2.67 lakh tons (+23% YoY, +17% QoQ); revenue INR1,941 crores (+38% YoY); EBITDA INR103 crores and PBT INR75 crores. Exports about 65,000 tons (+64% YoY); value-added products about 48% of volume.

segments.name: Lighting and Consumer Durables
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR507 crores (+17% YoY, +11% QoQ); EBITDA INR40 crores (7.8% margin) and PBT INR28 crores. H1 revenue INR964 crores (+16%), H1 EBITDA INR76 crores (+8%). Management says EBITDA would have been about INR48 crores excluding EPR liability (INR3-3.5 crores) and higher publicity spend (INR4-5 crores).

guidance_outlook: Steel: FY27 volume target of 11 lakh tons (H2 about 6 lakh tons), with exports at 22-25% of volumes; management said it will cross 11 lakh tons.

Steel EBITDA/ton: about INR4,800-4,900 in Q3 FY27 and above INR5,000 in Q4; full-year average about INR4,600-4,650. Management called INR5,000 the sustainable level, not a new normal of INR4,000-4,500.
Steel FY28: about 14 lakh tons at EBITDA/ton of INR4,600-4,800; about 2 million tons by FY2030.
Lighting FY27: value growth 22-23% and about 25% volume growth, about INR2,200 crores revenue and INR200 crores EBITDA; professional luminaire sales about INR600 crores.
Lighting FY28: about 20% value growth; about 15% revenue CAGR through FY30 with EBITDA margin of about 9-9.5%. Management said double-digit margin is possible in another year or two.

Capex: INR150-155 crores in FY27 (about INR50 crores spent by October); about INR75 crores in FY28 for Hindupur Phase 2; greenfield plant of INR250-300 crores to add 3-3.5 lakh tons, location in Vizag or Maharashtra to be decided in 2-3 months.
capex_capacity: Current steel capacity about 14.5 lakh tons; post-investment capacity about 2 million tons or slightly more.

Mill installed at Bhuj (DFT) already commissioned; new mills at Bahadurgarh and Gwalior (about INR55 crores each); Hindupur expansion on adjacent land (INR50-55 crores) to be commissioned by March FY27.
Greenfield project to be executed over about 2 years, with completion in phases at end of next year and the subsequent year; location to be near a port for imports.
Wire business: about INR95-100 crores done so far, FY27 target INR250 crores, FY28 target INR500 crores; almost 100% in-house production.
demand_pricing: Steel EBITDA/ton pressure attributed to freight (sea freight up about INR1,700/ton) and fixed-price export and API contracts, while trade pricing passes through price increases quickly.

API pipes: domestic API order book about 20,000 metric tons; margin per ton fell to about INR8,000 from about INR10,000 due to coating material costs, expected to settle in 2-3 months. Only 4-5 mills in India.
Export order book about 1 lakh tons worth INR850 crores (about 80,000 tons API); American orders of INR850-900 crores; steel prices about INR62,000/ton, expected INR60,000-64,000 until March.
Lighting: professional lighting order book above INR200 crores (includes about 25% maintenance); management says industry faces price erosion and most peers not achieving double-digit growth.
Section and square pipe segment growing 18-20% across India, but EBITDA about INR2,500-2,600/ton due to pricing pressure.

qa_highlights.question: Will steel EBITDA of about INR4,000-4,500/ton be the new normal, versus earlier guidance above INR5,500?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not a new normal; Q3 is expected at INR4,800-4,900/ton and Q4 above INR5,000, with the sustainable level around INR5,000 and the full year about INR4,600-4,650.

qa_highlights.question: Why is there no share buyback given the debt-free position and flat EPS?
qa_highlights.answer: The MD said a buyback is in the plans and a Board announcement could come by the next Board meeting or before it; no timeline was committed.

qa_highlights.question: What are the capex plans and greenfield economics?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex of INR150-155 crores; FY28 about INR75 crores for Hindupur Phase 2; greenfield INR250-300 crores (land included) adds 3-3.5 lakh tons, with the same product mix of 48-50% value-added.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 70% jump in other expenses?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to freight, with publicity also contributing, while some administrative expenses fell slightly.

qa_highlights.question: How does management see lighting margins and H2 given commodity pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited pan-India distribution, in-house manufacturing, pre-booking of imported materials 3-4 months ahead and cost control; it expects H2 to be better, with margins above 9% as a minimum target.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EPR impact and tax outflow?
qa_highlights.answer: EPR cost about INR3-3.5 crores in H1 and about INR5-6 crores a year going forward; advance tax paid about INR60 crores in H1 FY27, partly offset by refunds from the prior year.

risks_watch: Steel EBITDA/ton recovery to INR4,800-5,000+ in H2 depends on pass-through of price increases and freight normalisation; Q2 was about INR4,100.
Lighting margin pressure from commodity inflation (copper, aluminium, steel, petroleum-based inputs), price erosion, and unorganised competition; FY28 margin target of 9-9.5% is a stretch.
API pipe margin per ton has fallen from about INR10,000 to about INR8,000; management expects stabilisation in 2-3 months.
Capital allocation: buyback and demerger were raised by an analyst and remain undecided; management said a Board decision could come before the next Board meeting.
Greenfield plant location (Vizag or Maharashtra) and timing to be decided in 2-3 months; execution risk over about 2 years.
Wire business margin pressure and copper sensitivity; rising SKU count in kitchenware, coolers and plastic pipes with lighting ROCE about 14.2%.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volumes and order book, with steel EBITDA/ton recovery guided to H2 and buyback/demerger questions answered with commitments to talk to the Board rather than firm decisions. Cautious on lighting margins, citing industry pricing pressure and a longer timeline to double-digit margins.

rows.label: Export and API order book
